correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs first-Hermite complex-polynomial STFT under normalized Lebesgue phase-space measure. Its incomplete-gamma integrals give an exact signed adjacent eigenvalue difference and isolate the three-dimensional integer-area Fermi plateau by strict outer gaps. Differentiating the area-preserving elliptic boundary in trace norm and performing the exact degree-two angular selection yields the off-diagonal derivative -p_N sqrt(N/(N+1)); an isolated finite spectral projection then gives three sharp first-order branches and opposite limiting optimizer lines. The supplied Python checker independently integrates the matrix and passed 252 assertions for 7 sizes; checks supplement, not replace, the general proof. Fixed N is essential.

value.rationale: Maximal-rank spectral truncations are canonical finite Weyl–Heisenberg ensembles, so nonuniqueness of the exact rank-N Fermi projection is an operator-selection issue rather than an arbitrary invariant. The theorem gives a natural and exact resolution by a physically/geometrically motivated equal-area anisotropy, exposes opposite limiting maximizers for the two ellipse orientations, and computes the sharp gap-opening rate and isolated plateau margins. It distinguishes a structural degeneracy from generic perturbative splitting, but does not claim uniform-N estimates or a global shape optimum.
